Funny Looking Rock photograph a key → print a spare

↗ 2.5D tool
How to shoot it

Shoot square-on (straight above, key flat), shoulder and cuts visible. Use Rotate/Mirror/Flip to orient it roughly level, bow to one side. A card behind the key is optional (see Scale).

Why a card

Place a standard ID-card-sized rectangle behind the key. Because its real dimensions are known, the four corners let the app correct both scale and perspective skew — so even an off-square photo reads true. (Square-on with no card also works; scale then comes from the cut spacing.)

🔒 Keys often share a keychain, lanyard, or retractor with an ID badge or key-tag (gym membership, rewards, work ID). Don't let those into the same photo — a picture that shows both a key and who/where it belongs to is a real security risk. Take them off first, and store ID tags separately from your keys.

Aligning the box

Cards have rounded corners, so don't aim the handles at the corners — line up the box's edges with the card's straight sides. The corners sit where those edges would meet.

The card is optional — skip straight to Trace and the scale comes from the cut spacing.

How to trace (green / red)
  • Green = back edge: drag its ends onto the blade's straight back (depth zero).
  • Red per cut: drag into the valley — left/right onto the cut, up/down to its floor.

Red = matches a depth cleanly. Orange = between depths — nudge until red.

Scroll to zoom, drag empty area to pan. Pick the matching blank up top first.

—
Reading direction & keygen

The green arrow points to the tip; cut #1 is read from the bow end. Wrong way round? Flip reverses it.

⚠ Reading direction is per-keyway. This app numbers bow→tip. keygen uses the same bow→tip order for Schlage, so Schlage codes transfer directly. BEST/SFIC is the exception — it's numbered tip→bow — so reverse the code for BEST keys (in keygen or off a BEST spec sheet).

Know the code? Type it to skip the photo.

Marked on the bow, clear of the hole; a small fixed size. Tip down reads right on a keyring; Tip up on a retractor. Print the up face up.

Print flat on the bed (cuts in-plane), PETG/nylon/resin — a spare, not a daily key. Only copy keys you're authorized to. 🔒 Keep keys private.

Backup plan

The printed key is a working spare — and a physical backup of the key itself. Lose the original and a locksmith or key-cutting kiosk can cut a fresh metal key from your 3D print (or just from the bitting code you decoded — write it down). Keep the print or the code safe.
